newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus Amax sees balanced molybdenum market.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax sees balanced molybdenum market.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals, the world's biggest molybdenum producer, said it dipped into stocks to meet sales commitments last year as the market moved into balance.

"With the draw down of inventories that have taken place in the business, it seems to be in balance, the market right now," Milton Ward, Cyprus' president, chairman and chief executive told an analyst briefing on Wednesday.
Last year Cyprus produced 56 million pounds of molybdenum and sold 63 million pounds, taking 7 million pounds from its own inventory.
The company has two primary moly mines in Colorado, Henderson underground, which is operational, and the Climax surface mine, now on stand-by.
Moly is also produced as a by-product at Cyprus' Arizona copper mine.
Industry officials peg western world moly production at about 225 million pounds a year.
"We are going to be investing quite a bit of money in due course in our Henderson mine to make it more productive and reduce costs," Ward said.
"We feel good about the business and it is a business we are pleased to be in and we are going to continue to grow," Ward added.
Due to lower moly prices in 1996, income from by-product credits were 19 cents per pound lower than in 1995, Cyprus said.

Cyprus remains cautious about predicting moly prices. Last month it paid $3.6 million to Erie Forge and Steel to settle out of court a class action lawsuit which alleged price fixing. Erie was a consumer of molybdenum.
"Our position is that it was cheaper to settle than have a protracted lawsuit," a Cyprus spokesman said. "But we admit no wrongdoing."
The lawsuit covered a period from January 1 1991 to November 10, 1993 before Cyprus Minerals and Climax merged on November 15, 1993.
